title: Traffic fencing & namespace keys overview - Solaris Payments
summary: Redwood demo focused on namespace (org/project) key patterns, traffic fencing strategies to protect mission-critical payment flows, and how the Console + Optimize recommendations reduce token cost while preserving SLOs. Customer wants pilot with VPC control plane and an initial quota plan for high-value payment endpoints.
topics: billing segmentation for payment vs non-payment traffic
pilot next steps and benchmark plan
action_items: Maya Chen - Share pricing band for Dedicated reserved pool + pilot discount - due 2025-09-15
Liam O'Connor - Create a short benchmark script and sample payloads for their high-throughput payment route - due 2025-09-18
Elena Russo - Send list of compliance docs they need (SOC2 scoping + KMS integration questions) - due 2025-09-16
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot proposal and scope (dedicated capacity, VPC option, SLA targets)
Schedule a 60m pilot kickoff next Wed (attach benchmark sheet)
Customer to provide sample traffic profile and current per-route P95 latency
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-11 15:00 UTC — Duration 47m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor (Redwood); Priya Nair, Jonas Meyer, Elena Russo (Solaris Payments)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for carving out time. quick agenda: show how we do namespace keys and traffic fencing in the Console, then a look at Optimize recommendations for cost/latency, and close with pilot options.
00:14 Priya: hi thanks, very interested specifically in protecting our payment path — we have two types of calls: auth and non-auth, and auth must be highest priority and never starve.
00:28 Liam: totally, that's a common pattern. we'll show an approach where payment endpoints get a dedicated project key mapped to a reserved capacity lane — think of it as a "payment lane" that is fenced off from general traffic.
00:42 Jonas: quick Q — is that done by org vs project keys or by route-level policies? we've tried header-based routing before but had token leakage across services.
00:58 Liam: great question. recommended pattern is org-level umbrella + project keys per product line; you can then attach quotas and concurrency fences at the project key. that avoids token reuse issues. side note: we also have sticky-routing so traffic for a key prefers the same pool for cache locality.
01:20 Elena: and how does that play with burst behaviour? e.g., during flash sales we see spikes, we don't want payment verification to be throttled.
01:35 Maya: right, we demo two levers — reserved pools for guaranteed throughput and burst fencing. reserved pool keeps baseline capacity, and burst policy allows limited overflow to a lower-priority lane but with hard fallbacks. idea is to keep auth traffic first-class.
01:52 Jonas: can you show console now?
02:05 Liam: switching to screen share, Console -> Keys -> Create Project Key. ok, here we create "payments-prod-key" under org Solaris. you can set concurrency cap, token-per-second quotas, and attach it to a dedicated GPU pool.
02:28 Liam: notice the policy editor, we define a "payment-lane" tag and set routing preference: latency-first, fallback to cheaper model only if capacity exhausted. small typo in the UI here — it says 'fallbak' sometimes in internal builds — ignore that.
02:49 Priya: latency-first and fallback — what's the SLA we can expect if we do reserved dedicated?
03:02 Maya: with Dedicated pool and canary routing we typically hit p95 under 150ms for our optimized open models on A100-style hardware. of course depends on sequence length.
03:18 Jonas: sequence length for us is small — 128 tokens typically — so that sounds good.
03:30 Liam: also showed is KV cache affinity; if you route the same key to a pool, the KV cache warms and improves tail latency. note: some transcription in our demo recordings says KV "cash" at times.
03:47 Elena: security stuff — does this require us to hand over keys to Redwood? we need KMS/HSM integration and on-prem options.
04:01 Maya: you don't hand over customer keys; for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS. our Private control plane can be VPC-hosted with optional on-prem connectors and audit logs shipped to your SIEM.
04:20 Elena: do you provide pre-signed attestations or certs for SOC2?
04:29 Maya: we provide SOC2 artifact package and can run a security workshop for your compliance team. we'll include details in the package.
04:40 Jonas: let's talk costs — separate billing for the reserved pool plus per-token usage?
04:49 Maya: yes, pilot pricing typically bundles reserved capacity commit for the pool plus usage for overflow. Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and batching parameters to reduce token spend on non-critical routes.
05:05 Priya: can Optimize also suggest per-route config? we have a mixture of high-value payment calls and low-value analytics calls on same org.
05:18 Liam: Optimize will analyze traces and suggest per-model/route batching and quantization. for example, payments route we keep fp16 and lower latency kernels; analytics routes we suggest int8 quantization and larger batch sizes.
05:35 Jonas: any caveats about real-time compliance? we can't batch payment auth beyond micro-batching.
05:45 Liam: understood — Optimize respects per-route SLOs; suggestions flagged with expected delta in p95 and cost. you can accept or reject per-route.
06:05 Priya: can we create a sandbox org to test routing policies? don't want production impact.
06:12 Maya: yes we recommend a sandbox org + project keys mirror of prod. we'll provide a starter config that includes a payments key, analytics key, with quota baselines.
06:28 Priya: great. show me the console traffic visualization.
06:35 Liam: metrics tab — you can see token-level breakdown by key, latency heatmap, and a cost attribution view. here's a synthetic demo where we shift 20% of load to analytics lane and see cost drop 18% while p95 for payments stays flat.
07:05 Jonas: is routing programmable via API? we'd like to integrate with our feature flags to do rapid routing changes.
07:15 Liam: yes — API supports policy CRUD and route overrides. we'll share a sample script that does a canary re-route and rollbacks.
07:28 Priya: what about multi-region? we have EU and US data residency needs.
07:36 Maya: you can pin a project key to a region; fallback routing can be region-aware. for EU-restricted keys, traffic stays within EU pools.
07:49 Elena: any customers using this pattern in production? references?
07:57 Maya: we have a payments gateway reference (SanctumPay) that uses dedicated keys for auth and reporting keys for analytics; happy to connect you.
08:10 Jonas: about token leakage earlier — what prevents developers from copying keys into shared services?
08:22 Liam: RBAC + service tokens. recommend using short-lived tokens for services and use project keys for external clients only. Console shows active token usage per principal so you can revoke at any time.
08:40 Priya: what about throttling during high load — do you recommend soft or hard throttles?
08:48 Liam: a mix. hard throttles for payment auth when capacity is exhausted — but with burst policy you can allow a controlled number of requests to overflow to a billed, lower-priority lane with degraded model.
09:05 Maya: let's walk through a sample pilot: 2-week test, reserved pool sized to 2x current p95 capacity, benchmarking harness from Liam, and a Canary plan to move 5% traffic then 25% then full.
09:24 Jonas: sounds reasonable. do you need PROD credentials?
09:30 Priya: we'd rather start with mirrored traffic and synthetic load.
09:36 Liam: that's fine — we'll provide a harness that replays anonymized traces.
09:44 Elena: please include the security questionnaire answers.
09:48 Maya: noted — action item for Elena to list compliance docs they need.
09:55 Jonas: any limitations on concurrency caps per key?
10:00 Liam: you can set per-key concurrency caps and project-level hard limits. we also have fairshare algorithms for shared pools.
10:12 Priya: curious — if we run out of capacity in region, what's the fallback chain?
10:20 Liam: fallback chain: local reserved pool -> cross-region compatible pool (if allowed by policy) -> cheaper model variant (quantized) -> queued/throttled. all configurable per key.
10:36 Jonas: what about audit logs for every request? retention?
10:44 Maya: request-level metadata is logged and can be routed to your SIEM; retention configurable based on your tier.
10:53 Elena: sample SLA language?
10:57 Maya: we'll include SLA clause examples in the pilot proposal.
11:04 Priya: ok, recap please?
11:08 Maya: recap: 1) pattern: org umbrella + project keys per product area; 2) reserved payment lane + burst fencing; 3) Optimize to tune per-route configs; 4) pilot: sandbox replay + 2-week reserved pool benchmark; 5) deliverables: pricing, security pack, benchmark harness.
11:32 Jonas: thanks, next steps on our side: provide sample payloads and desired P95 targets.
11:38 Maya: we'll email pilot doc and calendar invite for kickoff.
11:45 Elena: thanks all.
11:48 Meeting ends.
